<objective>
Replace `compare-modal`'s `setTimeout(100)` layout guess with a `ResizeObserver` on the element it actually measures, plus mark-pending semantics so an early recalculation request is deferred rather than dropped (D-06, D-07, D-09).

Purpose: RACE-02. `calculateDefaultPositions()` measures `#comparisonCanvas`, but the only `ResizeObserver` in the component watches a DIFFERENT element, `#comparisonCenter`. Nothing observes the element being measured, which is why the code wraps the whole calculation in a 100ms timer and then silently gives up with `if (canvasHeight === 0) return;`. The timer is a guess; the early-return is a dropped request.

Output: cached canvas dimensions fed by a dedicated observer, a synchronous `calculateDefaultPositions()`, a pending-recalc flag that closes the race, and a spec proving the deferred path runs.
</objective>

## Scope boundary — read before touching anything

`calculateImageDimensions()` and its `POSITION_BUFFER = 40` are NOT in scope (D-09). That buffer is
load-bearing and documented in `.claude/CLAUDE.md` ("Compare Modal Image Rendering Fix") and PROJECT.md:
`image-display`'s `.display-container` has 20px padding per side, so without the 40px added to both the
container width and height the content area can shrink to zero at small scales and clip the image. This
plan changes only where `calculateDefaultPositions()` gets its canvas dimensions from — a different
method. The existing `Image Dimensions with Buffer` specs must keep passing untouched.

  <behavior>
    - Calling `calculateDefaultPositions()` when no canvas dimensions have been observed yet leaves `leftTransform`/`rightTransform` unchanged and records a pending request.
    - Feeding non-zero canvas dimensions afterwards runs the deferred calculation exactly once and updates `leftTransform`/`rightTransform`.
    - Calling `calculateDefaultPositions()` when canvas dimensions are already known updates the transforms synchronously, within the same tick, with no timer advance.
    - Feeding canvas dimensions when nothing is pending does not itself trigger a recalculation (the existing triggers stay the only drivers, per D-06).
    - Given a 1000x800 canvas and 200x300 left/right image dimensions, the computed transforms match the current algorithm's output for the same inputs.
  </behavior>
  <action>
Rewrite how `CompareModalComponent` obtains the canvas dimensions used by `calculateDefaultPositions()`.

<!-- planner-discipline-allow: setTimeout -->

Add four private fields next to the existing `resizeObserver` field (~line 74):
- `private canvasDimensions = { width: 0, height: 0 };`
- `private canvasResizeObserver?: ResizeObserver;`
- `private observedCanvasEl: HTMLElement | null = null;`
- `private pendingDefaultPositionsRecalc = false;`

Add `private onCanvasResize(width: number, height: number): void`. It assigns
`this.canvasDimensions = { width, height }`, and then — only if `this.pendingDefaultPositionsRecalc`
is true AND `height > 0` — clears the flag and calls `this.runDefaultPositionsCalc()`. Extracting the
observer's body into this named method is deliberate: it gives the spec a deterministic way to simulate
layout without depending on the browser firing a real resize (the Karma global `ResizeObserver` stub in
`src/test-setup.ts` has a no-op `observe()`).

Add `private syncCanvasObserver(): void`. Let `el = this.comparisonCanvas?.nativeElement ?? null`.
If `el === this.observedCanvasEl`, return immediately (this method runs on every change-detection pass,
so the no-op path must be trivially cheap). Otherwise: disconnect `this.canvasResizeObserver` if it
exists, reset `this.canvasDimensions` to `{ width: 0, height: 0 }`, set
`this.observedCanvasEl = el`, and — if `el` is non-null — construct a new `ResizeObserver` whose
callback iterates `entries` and calls
`this.onCanvasResize(entry.contentRect.width, entry.contentRect.height)`, then `observe(el)`.
This element-identity re-sync is required because `#comparisonCanvas` sits inside an `@if` on both
models being selected: it does not exist when `ngAfterViewInit` first runs, and it is destroyed and
recreated whenever a model is cleared and re-selected.

Wire `syncCanvasObserver()` into two places:
- At the end of `ngAfterViewInit`, AFTER the existing `comparisonCenter` observer block. Leave that
  existing block byte-for-byte unchanged — D-06 is explicit that the existing recalculation triggers
  (the panel-state subscription at lines 88-97 and the `comparisonCenter` observer) both keep calling
  `calculateDefaultPositions()` exactly as they do today.
- In a new `ngAfterViewChecked()` hook (add `AfterViewChecked` to the class's `implements` clause and to
  the `@angular/core` import list), whose entire body is `this.syncCanvasObserver();`. This is what
  attaches the observer at the moment the canvas element first appears, without a timer.

Rewrite `calculateDefaultPositions()` (currently lines 603-654) to be synchronous:
- Remove the deferring timer wrapper entirely and the `const canvas = this.comparisonCanvas?.nativeElement`
  measurement inside it.
- New body: if `this.canvasDimensions.height === 0`, set `this.pendingDefaultPositionsRecalc = true` and
  return (D-07 — mark pending, never silently drop). Otherwise call `this.runDefaultPositionsCalc()`.

Add `private runDefaultPositionsCalc(): void` containing the current calculation body verbatim
(today's lines 610-651), with exactly two changes: read `const canvasWidth = this.canvasDimensions.width;`
and `const canvasHeight = this.canvasDimensions.height;` from the cache instead of from
`canvas.clientWidth`/`canvas.clientHeight`, and drop the now-redundant zero-height early return (the
caller guards it). Everything else — the `this.calculateImageDimensions()` call at the top, the
`|| 200` / `|| 240` fallbacks, `padding = 10`, `gap = 20`, the fits-side-by-side vs. overlap branch, the
`defaultLeftPosition`/`defaultRightPosition` assignments, and the two `translate(...)` transform strings —
must be preserved exactly. Per `.claude/skills/scaling-system/SKILL.md` this is pixel-space layout math;
do not "improve" any of it.

In `ngOnDestroy`, add `this.canvasResizeObserver?.disconnect();` next to the existing
`this.resizeObserver.disconnect()` call, and null out `this.observedCanvasEl`.

Do NOT touch `calculateImageDimensions()`, its `POSITION_BUFFER = 40`, `onDragStart`, `canvasRect`, or
the `@HostListener('document:mousemove')`-based panel drag at lines 500-534 — that drag is explicitly
out of scope per D-05 (Angular tears host listeners down on destroy, so it does not leak).

After this task, exactly ONE deferred-timer call remains in this file: the one inside
`applyDefaultOverlays` (~line 235), which plan 03-07 removes as part of D-08. Do not remove it here —
it belongs to a different fix with its own service-side API change.
  </action>
